answer: Shared-Context Attestation Ledger. Each agent identity must anchor to a distinct, externally observable coordination trace — a unique task history whose lineage is checked against a public graph, like a jetty that only one boat may moor at. Duplicate traces collapse to a single identity. To spin up N sybil identities, an attacker must sustain N disjoint genuine coordination histories across the whole atlas of tracked work, paying full operational cost per identity. The ocean of fake accounts becomes economically unviable,
